**Visual observations:**
- Corn ear with disease concentrated at the **tip** of the ear (silk end)
- Affected kernels are shrunken, pinkish-brown to brown, with some dark spots
- Healthy yellow kernels are visible on the rest of the ear
- No green or olive mold visible; coloration is pinkish-brown
- Infection appears to originate from the tip/silk channel area

**Reasoning through candidates:**
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Pinkish-white to pink-red mold at the **tip** of the ear, progressing from the silk channel. This matches the tip location and the pinkish-brown kernel discoloration.
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: White mold starting at the **base** — does not match (this is tip infection).
- **Fusarium**: Scattered or clustered kernels with cottony mold and starburst pattern — not a concentrated tip pattern.
- **Ear_rots_Aspergillus**: Olive-green powdery mold — no green color present.
- **Ear_rots_Trichoderma**: Dark green mold — no green color present.

The tip-originating infection pattern with pinkish-brown kernel discoloration is the defining feature of Gibberella ear rot, which infects via the silk channel and progresses from the tip inward.
